title: の: A の B
meaning_en: B belonging to A; A's B.
explanation: の links two nouns. The first noun owns or describes the second: わたし の さいふ (my wallet), にほんご の ほん (a Japanese book).
The thing owned can be dropped when it is obvious: この かさ は わたし の です ("this umbrella is mine"). To ask who owns it say だれ の です か.
You can chain の: わたし の はは の かばん is "my mother's bag".
common_mistakes: Putting the thing before の (the owner goes first).
Using は where の is needed.

title: も: also
explanation: も replaces は and adds "also, too": わたし も がくせい です (I am a student too).
Use X も Y も for "both": ちち も はは も いしゃ です.
Do not use both は and も for the same word.
common_mistakes: Using も when the second item is different in kind.

title: じゃ ありません: is not
pattern: X は Y じゃ ありません
explanation: The polite negative of です is じゃ ありません. わたし は いしゃ じゃ ありません = I am not a doctor.
In careful writing and speech you may also hear では ありません; じゃ is the everyday form.
To ask a negative question add か, and to answer use いいえ.
structure_notes: Topic は noun じゃ ありません.
common_mistakes: Forgetting じゃ and saying ありません only.
Mixing positive です with いいえ.
